title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (recapitulated on the next page): X is a scheme of finite type over Q-bar. D = sum_{i in I} D_i is an effective divisor with smooth components, and X is smooth at the generic (maximal) points of supp D. Put X' = X - D. G_{X'} is the discrete group of all scheme automorphisms of X preserving D (and later a set J of points). These automorphisms are semilinear: they map to Gamma = Aut(Q-bar/Q) through their action on constants. E_{X'} is the extension of G_{X'} by pi_1(X') obtained by lifting automorphisms to the profinite universal cover, so 1 -> pi_1(X') -> E_{X'} -> G_{X'} -> 1. The previous page gives the outer action G_{X'} -> Autext(pi_1(X'), T(Q-bar), (phi_i)). Here T(Q-bar) = lim mu_n = Z-hat(1), and the phi_i are 'structures Kummériennes'.

This page rigidifies that outer action into an actual equivariant structure. Let X~' be the normalisation of X in the universal pro-cover of X'. Let X~'(I) be the set of points of X~' over the generic points of the D_i. X~'(i) is the fibre over D_i; it is a homogeneous space under pi_1(X'), and its elements are the 'cusps' or branches of the universal cover above D_i.

(22) For each such point x, the inertia group at x is canonically Kummer-isomorphic to T(Q-bar) = Z-hat(1). This is because the residue characteristic is 0 and all roots of unity lie in Q-bar. This gives phi_i: X~'(i) -> Hom(T(Q-bar), pi_1(X')), equivariant for pi_1(X') acting by translation on the source and by conjugation on the target. The faint words 'compatible avec les opérations de pi_1(X') de part et d'autre' express this. The construction makes precise the conjugacy-class data used in (17).

(23) The whole family phi = (phi_i) is a map X~'(I) -> Hom(T(Q-bar), pi_1(X')) that is equivariant for the larger group E_{X'}. On the target, E_{X'} acts by conjugation on pi_1(X') and also on T(Q-bar) via E -> G -> Gamma, i.e. through the cyclotomic character. This is the equivariant (non-outer) form of 'cuspidal inertia structure'.

(5) Next, Grothendieck adds a set J of Q-bar-points of X'. X~'(J) is its inverse image in the universal cover, i.e. the fibre-functor points, homogeneous over each point under pi_1. G' is the subgroup of G_{X'}(I) stabilising J. G' and its preimage E' act compatibly on J, on X~'(J), and on the projection (24) X~'(J) -> J.

The next page completes this. A lift of a point x in J gives a partial splitting Psi_J: X~'(J) -> Hom(G'_J, E') over the stabiliser G'_J. These are the sections attached to rational points, in the style of the section conjecture.

The point of the whole construction is a 'paradigm': the full set of combinatorial and arithmetic data a profinite fundamental group should carry so that (X, D, J) can be reconstructed. That data is: inertia at cusps with a cyclotomic twist, and sections from marked points, all equivariant for one extension combining geometric automorphisms and Galois.
errors: No mathematical error. Two implicit points need to be stated. First, the inertia at a point of X~' over the generic point of D_i is identified with Z-hat(1) of the residue field. This equals T(Q-bar) only because the base is Q-bar, which contains all roots of unity. Second, phi_i is injective onto a procyclic subgroup only when that inertia is nontrivial; this holds since X' is the complement of D.
The marginal note itself flags a gap: X' = X - D has to be stated before X~'(I) is defined. Grothendieck adds this on the recapitulation page.

ideas.what: Equivariant map from the cusps of the universal cover to inertia homomorphisms Z-hat(1) -> pi_1, with pi_1 acting by conjugation
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia subgroups / tame inertia structure (Kummer structure) of the fundamental group of an open variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental group); anabelian use by Nakamura and Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: SGA1 and Grothendieck–Murre on the tame fundamental group; the anabelian use is implicit in the letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Compatibility of the inertia maps with the full arithmetic–geometric extension E, with the action on T(Q-bar) through Gamma (cyclotomic character)
ideas.modern_name: Galois-equivariance of cuspidal inertia; cyclotomic twist of inertia

ideas.what: Using the discrete group of all semilinear scheme automorphisms of (X, D, J) instead of the Galois group alone, and its extension by pi_1
ideas.modern_name: extension of the automorphism group of a pointed or punctured variety by its fundamental group (mapping-class / Teichmüller-type setting, arithmetic version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower programme (Esquisse); Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses related ideas, but not this exact formalism

ideas.what: A marked set J of rational points giving partial splittings over its stabiliser
ideas.modern_name: sections attached to rational points (section conjecture), including sections over stabilisers

missed.claim: This is an explicit 'paradigm' formalism. It packages cuspidal inertia (with cyclotomic twist) and rational-point sections into a single equivariant structure for one extension E of the group of all semilinear automorphisms of (X, D, J). It is stated for X of arbitrary finite type over Q-bar, not only for curves. Similar packages exist in later anabelian work (Mochizuki's cuspidal and inertia data, Nakamura). However, this simultaneous equivariant formalism with geometric automorphisms and an arbitrary-dimensional setting does not appear in this form in Grothendieck's published texts.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck around 1980-81 already treated decorated fundamental groups equivariantly, combining automorphisms and Galois. This is useful historically. Mathematically it is largely subsumed by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but largely standard rigidification: inertia at cusps, the cyclotomic twist, and sections from points. It is historically interesting as an early, general formulation of the anabelian data package, but a specialist would recognise all its ingredients.
transcription_corrections: In (22) the target is Hom(T(Q̄), π_1(X')), not Hom(J(Q̄), ...).

The faint line 'compatible avec les opérations de π_1(X')' appears to be faded ink rather than a deletion. Read together with the next line it gives 'compatible avec les opérations de π_1(X') de part et d'autre'.
In (23) 'compatible avec les E_{X'} de [?] et d'autre' should read 'de part et d'autre'.
'Soit G_{X'}(I, J) ... G' le sous-groupe de G_{X'}(I) qui invarie J': the defined object is G', the stabiliser of J.
The marginal note reads roughly 'ici il faut aussi dire X' = X - D ... autrement ... le fait que ... X~(I) ... les points de X~' au-dessus des points maximaux ... X~'(I)'.
